editorial:
Leonard Shelby is a man on a mission, but his broken memory turns every clue into a fresh mystery. You follow him through notes, tattoos, and Polaroids as he hunts the man who hurt his wife, never sure who to trust. The story jumps backward and forward, so you piece together the truth right alongside him. It feels tense, clever, and surprisingly emotional, with strong performances that keep you locked in. Guy Pearce makes Leonard both tough and vulnerable, while Carrie-Anne Moss and Joe Pantoliano add sharp, uneasy energy.

The pacing is quick and the structure keeps you guessing, though the puzzle can feel confusing on first watch. If you like thrillers that reward close attention, this is a great pick. It is not a casual background movie, but it is a smart, gripping ride that stays with you after the credits.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Teddy tells Leonard that Jimmy was not the real killer and that Leonard has been chasing different "John G" suspects for a while. Leonard refuses to accept it, writes Teddy's license plate as a clue, and drives away, setting Teddy up as his next target. The twist is that Leonard may be lying to himself and repeating the cycle, choosing a new suspect instead of facing the truth.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves puzzle thrillers and twisty mysteries.
